channel.title: Man Group · Insights
channel.description: Original Man Institute now redirects to Man Insights. Public insight cards from the official successor, first page; month precision dates are not invented as exact days.

item.title: Risks and Opportunities in the Fog of the Credit Cycle
item.description: We believe this is a cycle characterised more by dispersion than broad-based credit deterioration.

item.title: Do Markets Have the Bandwidth for the Midterms?
item.description: Options markets currently price a quick US midterm election result. But a long count, or unrest, could test markets more than it did in 2021.

item.title: The Freedom of Not Doing It All
item.description: Inspired by a talk by Oliver Burkeman, author of Four Thousand Weeks , at the Man Alternative Investing Symposium, we explore how letting go of the need to control everything can help us focus on what matters now.

item.title: Professor Philip Stier, University of Oxford, on the Frontier of AI and Climate Science
item.description: Professor Philip Stier, University of Oxford and Director of the Intelligent Earth Centre, on how AI will change the way we understand climate risk.

item.title: Significantly Misunderstood: Why SRT is Not Capital Relief
item.description: In the first of a series, we aim to dispel the misconception that significant risk transfers (SRT) reduce the amount of regulatory capital a bank must hold.

item.title: AI Tokens: The Hot Commodity Whose Price Keeps Falling
item.description: AI tokens are the world’s newest commodity. But while they share the characteristics of coal, oil and electricity, they are uniquely deflationary. What is more, the market dynamics surrounding them reprice the value of intelligence itself.

item.title: The AI Bubble: Hidden Risks and Opportunities
item.description: AI technology is transformative and here to stay. But the inflated financial architecture supporting it may be unsustainable.

item.title: Under Pressure
item.description: Hedge fund strategies might need to brace for more volatility for the rest of the year.

item.title: Gold: Bugs, Bears and Myths
item.description: Despite reaching record prices, gold can play a valuable role in global portfolios as a diversifier and risk mitigator.

item.title: The Quant Renaissance Part III: Who's Ready for the Next Winter?
item.description: Did quant managers really change after the Quant Winter? Their returns say some did and some did not.

item.title: What If Gold Had a Yield?
item.description: Gold currently pays no income while 30-year Treasuries yield over 5%, but gold miners could narrow the gap.

item.title: The Assets Powering the Next Investment Cycle
item.description: Essential assets, long-term investment trends and the case for listed infrastructure today.

item.title: Bond Markets Price Political Dysfunction as Well as Debt
item.description: While sovereign debt crisis concerns may have eased for now, that’s no free bond market pass for profligate governments.

item.title: Weathering July's Storms
item.description: How have quant equity strategies fared amid China’s shifting equity market dynamics?

item.title: The Law of the Medes and Persians
item.description: Re-investigating three of investment's long-held rules.

item.title: Professor Alex Edmans, on the Madness of Markets… and Sustainable Investing
item.description: Professor Alex Edmans, London Business School, talks about why smart investors make crazy decisions — and how to exploit them.

item.title: What Are We Buying When We Buy Gold?
item.description: The debate rages on whether the yellow metal is just a hedge or something more.

item.title: Beyond Stock Selection: A Systematic Approach to EM Country Timing
item.description: Emerging markets (EM) systematic managers now have the potential to reinforce stock selection with a complementary country timing component

item.title: Taking an Active Approach in Today’s Fixed Income Market
item.description: As hyperscalers pile into the corporate bond market, unintentional concentration risk is also rising.

item.title: Don’t Write Off Bonds Yet
item.description: Elevated inflation alone is not bad for Treasuries; it takes rapidly rising inflation to drive bonds down.

item.title: Deglobalisation: Insights on a Regime Shift
item.description: The era of neoliberal globalism has peaked, giving way to a populist age of deglobalisation. This regime shift brings profound effects, not least on investor portfolios.

item.title: The Art of Being Ready
item.description: In the first of our 2026 Man Alternative Investing Symposium insights series, we consider what investors can learn from emergency planning. Inspired by a talk from Lucy Easthope, a leading authority on recovering from disaster, we explore why preparation is key, from rehearsing difficult decisions to making space for dissent.
